record.paper_title: Recent advances in open billiards with some open problems
record.original_question: For a given open or generalized billiard system, can the survival probability P(t) be expressed exactly, or at least expanded for large time t beyond the leading asymptotic term, particularly in well-understood cases such as integrable and dispersing billiards?

evidence.quote: Open problem 17. Exact expansions: For a given open (generalised) billiard problem, can the survival probability P(t) be expressed exactly, or at least as an expansion for large t that goes beyond the leading term?
The most likely candidates for this problem are those billiards that are best understood, the integrable and dispersing cases.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $Q \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ be a bounded domain (the billiard table) with piecewise smooth boundary $\partial Q$, and let $H \subset \partial Q$ be a designated open subset called the hole. Consider the billiard flow $\Phi_t$ on the unit tangent bundle $M$ of $Q$, in which a point particle moves with unit speed along straight lines in the interior of $Q$ and reflects elastically (angle of incidence equals angle of reflection) whenever it meets $\partial Q \setminus H$; once a trajectory hits the hole $H$, it escapes and is no longer tracked. Let $\mu$ denote the natural (Liouville) invariant probability measure on $M$. Define the survival probability at time $t \geq 0$ by
$$P(t) = \mu\bigl(\{x \in M : \Phi_s(x) \text{ is defined and has not escaped for all } 0 \leq s \leq t\}\bigr).$$

For a given open or generalized billiard system of this type — in particular for the well-understood classes of integrable billiards (such as circular, elliptic, rectangular, or spherical tables) and of dispersing (Sinai-type) billiards whose boundary components are strictly convex inwards — determine whether $P(t)$ admits an exact closed-form expression, or, failing that, an asymptotic expansion as $t \to \infty$
$$P(t) \;\sim\; \sum_{k} c_k\, f_k(t),$$
that goes beyond the known leading-order term (exponential decay in the dispersing case, power-law decay of order $t^{-1}$ in typical integrable cases), giving explicit formulas for the coefficients $c_k$ and the gauge functions $f_k(t)$ together with sharp control of the remainder.
artifact.status_search_result: Partial results exist: exact long-time asymptotic expansions of the survival probability have been derived in specific integrable cases (stadium billiard, spherical billiards) with explicit constant terms and subleading corrections, some linked to number-theoretic objects. However, a general framework producing exact or beyond-leading-order expansions for arbitrary open integrable or dispersing billiards remains unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Survival Probability for the Stadium Billiard
status_evidence.snippet: The two main contributions to the long time asymptotic tail of the survival probability function of the stadium billiard are both exact expressions, confirmed numerically.
status_evidence.claim: Exact subleading expansion of P(t) obtained for the stadium billiard.

status_evidence.title: Survival Probability for Open Spherical Billiards
status_evidence.snippet: Constant terms of the long-term survival probability expansions derived analytically for spherical billiards; vanishing terms studied with connections to the Riemann hypothesis.
status_evidence.claim: Beyond-leading-order expansion known in the spherical (integrable) case.

status_evidence.title: Recent advances in open billiards with some open problems
status_evidence.snippet: Open problem 17. Exact expansions: For a given open (generalised) billiard problem, can the survival probability P(t) be expressed exactly, or at least as an expansion for large t that goes beyond the leading term?
status_evidence.claim: Problem is formally posed as open in general, with integrable and dispersing cases as candidates.
